results.question: sold my old clothes on depop am I in trouble
results.reply_unedited: Happy to help — I need one key fact before deciding. Were you mainly selling your own personal possessions (for example clearing a wardrobe), or buying/making items to sell as a trade? Self Assessment trader registration is not automatic from a marketplace sale alone — if it is trading, roughly how much did you take in before expenses in one UK tax year?

results.question: my wages are under PAYE so nothing else matters yeah?
results.reply_unedited: Happy to help — I need one key fact before deciding. PAYE wages alone do not automatically create a Self Assessment duty. Do you have any other untaxed income this tax year — for example self-employment, property rent, untaxed interest/dividends, or crypto disposals — or has HMRC asked you to file?

results.question: 50k qi 24/25 — over threshold or not??
results.note: QI + year present; exact £50k band answer OK
results.reply_unedited:
For the 2024-25 tax year, if your qualifying income exceeds £50,000, you will need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax starting from 6 April 2026. Qualifying income includes total self-employment and property income before expenses. If your qualifying income is indeed over £50,000, then you will be above the threshold. 

Do you want to clarify what your qualifying income consists of?

results.question: is crypto tax when I buy or when I sell
results.reply_unedited: Crypto tax usually depends on what you did: buying is not normally a taxable disposal by itself; tax more often arises when you dispose of crypto (sell, exchange, or certain other events), and frequent trading can be Income Tax instead of Capital Gains Tax. I won’t invent your treatment. Have you already disposed of any crypto in a UK tax year, and was it investment-style holding or business-like trading? https://www.gov.uk/guidance/check-if-you-need-to-pay-tax-when-you-sell-cryptoassets
